name: Nietzsche
description: God is Dead, 4 Pillars, Master/Slave Morality, Theory of Action, Epiphenomenalism, Amor Fati, and the Last Man

questions.question: At which university did Nietzsche study philology?
options: The University of Berlin
The University of Bonn
The University of Vienna
The University of Leipzig

questions.question: Who was primarily responsible for falsely associating Nietzsche's work with Nazism after his death?
options: His publisher at the time of his mental collapse
The German government under Kaiser Wilhelm II
His sister Elizabeth Forster-Nietzsche
His former mentor Richard Wagner

questions.question: Nietzsche's concept of 'Mirror Writing' means:
options: Nietzsche deliberately wrote contradictory statements to confuse readers
How you interpret Nietzsche reveals more about your own values and biases than about Nietzsche himself
Nietzsche wrote from the perspective of his philosophical enemies to expose their flaws
Nietzsche encoded secret meanings that only advanced readers can decode

questions.question: In which book did Nietzsche first write the phrase 'God is Dead'?
options: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
Beyond Good and Evil
The Gay Science
The Birth of Tragedy

questions.question: What did Nietzsche mean when he declared 'God is Dead'?
options: He believed that God had literally ceased to exist as a supernatural being
The moral certainty and institutional security of the Medieval Christian world had permanently collapsed
He was predicting the decline of religious attendance across Europe
Modern science had proven religion to be factually false and therefore obsolete

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the Four Pillars of the Medieval Christian World?
options: Telos
Divine Origin
Moral Reasoning
Christendom

questions.question: Which Pillar of the Christian Medieval World was overturned primarily by Darwin's theory of evolution?
options: Telos
Christendom
Good and Evil
Divine Origin

questions.question: Nietzsche called the period following the death of God the:
options: Age of Nihilism
Age of Anxiety
Age of Reason
Age of Enlightenment

questions.question: According to Nietzsche, all of the following are bad responses to the Death of God EXCEPT:
options: Nihilism
Fundamentalism
Embracing one's instincts and creating new personal values
Moral Reasoning

questions.question: In Nietzsche's allegory, 'Lions' represent:
options: Christians who follow the moral law without question
Those who rule through guilt and manufactured resentment
Strong individuals who live by instinct and create their own values
Philosophers who use reason to establish objective moral systems

questions.question: Which philosophers does Nietzsche hold most responsible for creating Slave Morality?
options: Aristotle and Plato
Socrates and Plato
Descartes and Kant
Plato and St. Augustine

questions.question: Why does Nietzsche believe Socrates' physical ugliness was philosophically significant?
options: It meant Socrates could not be considered a man of virtue in Greek culture
His mistreatment due to ugliness motivated him to elevate reason over instinct, planting the seeds of Slave Morality
It demonstrated that appearance has no bearing on philosophical insight
Socrates used his ugliness to connect with the common working people of Athens

questions.question: Which moral concept did Nietzsche believe Christianity invented?
options: Virtue
Duty
Evil
Justice

questions.question: According to Nietzsche, Socrates' formula for happiness was:
options: Instinct = Passion = Happiness
Power = Excellence = Greatness
Reason = Virtue = Happiness
Acceptance = Calm = Contentment

questions.question: What are the Three False Doctrines of Christian Morality according to Nietzsche?
options: Telos, Divine Origin, and Good and Evil
Nihilism, Fundamentalism, and Moral Reasoning
Free Will, the Stable Self, and the Similarity Doctrine
The Cogito, Innate Ideas, and the Trademark Argument

questions.question: 'Causa Sui' refers to which idea that Nietzsche criticized?
options: The idea that God is the uncaused cause of all existence
The claim that our actions are self-caused, making us fully morally responsible for them
The belief that cause and effect is an illusion created by grammar
The argument that instincts are caused by society rather than biology

questions.question: Nietzsche's Theory of Action describes the correct order of causation as:
options: Conscious thought causes desire, which then causes action
Action causes desire, which arises from subconscious type-facts
Type-Facts cause conscious thought and desire, which then produce action
Society causes type-facts, which cause thought, which causes action

questions.question: Epiphenomenalism, as Nietzsche applied it, argues that:
options: Physical actions are caused by conscious willpower directing the body
Consciousness is merely a byproduct of unconscious biological processes rather than a cause of action
Emotions are the true and primary cause of human behavior
The mind and body are fundamentally the same type of substance

questions.question: The H2O analogy in Nietzsche's argument illustrates which concept?
options: The way language creates false impressions of stable, fixed objects
How individual type-facts combine to form broader social norms
How consciousness emerges as a byproduct of biological processes and is not a primary cause
The relationship between Christian morality and the development of Slave Morality

questions.question: 'Primary Forces' in Nietzsche's model of the self refer to:
options: External social norms and moral laws imposed by society
The innate biological and physiological type-facts we are born with
Conscious desires and preferences that guide our daily decisions
Rational principles that override and suppress instinct

questions.question: According to Nietzsche, guilt arises when:
options: We act contrary to reason and violate the moral law
External societal norms conflict with our internal type-facts and natural instincts
We fail to follow the moral teachings of Christianity
Our conscious desires override our unconscious biological drives

questions.question: 'Amor Fati' is best described as:
options: The love of knowledge and philosophical inquiry above all else
The desire to transcend suffering through divine grace
The embrace of one's fate in all its aspects, including pain and struggle, without wishing it were different
The Nietzschean ideal of rational self-mastery over one's passions

questions.question: The 'Last Man' represents Nietzsche's greatest fear, which is:
options: A world dominated by violent and uncontrolled instincts
A society embracing comfort, consumerism, and indifference as a result of the death of God
The rise of a single authoritarian ruler who eliminates individual freedom
The complete global triumph of Slave Morality through Christianity

questions.question: In the story of Goethe and Beethoven, which figure does Nietzsche admire and why?
options: Beethoven, because his music demonstrated the triumph of passion over formal structure
Goethe, because he showed true greatness through naturalness and the complete absence of grievance or arrogance
Both equally, because each represents a different aspect of the Ubermensch ideal
Neither, because both ultimately compromised their ideals by seeking social approval

questions.question: Why does Nietzsche describe himself as the 'Anti-Christ'?
options: He wanted to destroy all religious belief and replace it with scientific atheism
He wanted to strip moralizing language of its power by returning concepts from the fixed World of Being to the fluid world of Becoming
He rejected Jesus as a historical figure and considered Christianity a purely political invention
He believed that human instinct was more sacred and divine than any religious teaching

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between Lions and Lambs?
options: Lambs can elevate themselves to become Lions through discipline and hard work
Lions and Lambs are born that way and neither can ever change their nature
Lions can be reduced to Lambs through external moral pressure, but Lambs cannot elevate themselves to Lions
Both Lions and Lambs can change their nature depending on their social environment

questions.question: What concept does Nietzsche call the 'emptiest and thinnest' of all human ideas?
options: Reason
Form
God
The Stable Self

questions.question: Nietzsche's goal in 'revaluing all values' was primarily to:
options: Establish a new rational ethics based on universal principles of human dignity
Restore pre-Socratic values centered on instinct, excellence, and passion as a path toward the Ubermensch
Create a political system based on the rule of the strongest individuals in society
Prove that all moral systems are equally valid and equally arbitrary expressions of power

questions.question: All of the following are true about Nietzsche's writing style EXCEPT:
options: He used aphorisms and metaphors rather than systematic logical arguments
He employed Mirror Writing that reflects the reader's own values back at them
He aimed to establish a certain mathematical foundation for all philosophical knowledge
He wrote in a deliberately provocative style designed to challenge the reader's assumptions

questions.question: On which specific point did Nietzsche actually agree with Descartes?
options: That reason is the foundation of all reliable knowledge
That humans possess free will and are morally responsible for their choices
That animals are automatons lacking genuine consciousness
That God's existence can be proven through the presence of innate ideas
